plans.includes: Every plan includes Hoody AI (free), the Hoody Kit, Bots and agents, the API, SDK and CLI, link permissions, disk encryption and full SSH access.
plans.cmp.title: Compare plans
plans.more.all.title: All plans
plans.more.all.toolsBody: Docker, Podman, Kubernetes and nearly any tool like them, on every plan.
plans.more.all.vmsBody: With their own kernel and OS, on bare metal only.
plans.more.all.sitesBody: As many sites as your computers can run. Connect your own domains, HTTPS included.
plans.more.bot.title: Bot URLs
plans.more.bot.lede: One shareable address for one Bot. Each person or agent gets its own named key.
plans.more.bot.peopleBody: Chat with your Bot directly on the web, at its link. No app, no install, no Hoody account.
plans.more.bot.agentsBody: Call it by API: OpenAI clients add /v1, Anthropic clients use it as is, MCP clients add /mcp.
plans.more.bot.withBody: Web chat, OpenAI, Anthropic and MCP clients
plans.more.bot.whyBody: Give your Bot to a teammate or another agent without sharing your account. Pause or revoke any key on its own. One shared conversation, every caller named in the log.
plans.more.ssh.title: Full SSH access
plans.more.ssh.keyBody: Add your public key to the computer. One key per computer; SFTP works too.
plans.more.ssh.browserBody: One link per terminal: terminal-1, terminal-2 and so on.
plans.more.ssh.cliBody: Opens terminal 1 in your browser. Add --url to print its link.
plans.more.ssh.noneBody: The Hoody CLI and Hoody Agent, run on our side and signed in. Reach your computers from there with ssh hoody.com.
plans.more.free.title: Free has useful limits
plans.more.free.lede: Enough to get your sites, Bots and projects running.
plans.more.free.computersBody: Full Linux computers with the Kit, Bots, API, SDK and CLI.
plans.more.free.sharedBody: Shared by your computers. Shared plans run on shared machines, so your computers share the network with other users.
plans.more.free.versionsBody: Take snapshots of your computers' storage and restore them in one step.
plans.more.free.aiBody: Included, rate-limited, with no key or prepaid AI Balance needed.
plans.more.free.growAi: Only paid AI is metered, by tokens, from the AI Balance you fund.
plans.more.free.yoursBody: Hoody claims no ownership of your files or code and never sells your data. Download folders as ZIP files, keep backups on your own Drive or S3, and leave any time.
plans.more.free.howLede: Shared hardware, clear limits. Keep independent copies.
plans.more.free.whoBody: One Free per person, subject to eligibility and capacity.
plans.more.free.hardwareBody: Hardware and kernel are shared with other users.
plans.more.free.limitsBody: Defaults can change; your account's live limits apply. New computers or snapshots are refused at their count caps.
plans.more.free.processesBody: Processes and threads are capped in total. At the cap, new processes fail to start; running tasks continue.
plans.more.free.emailBody: Outbound email (SMTP) is blocked by default.
plans.more.free.backupsBody: Hoody keeps no backups of Free storage. Keep independent copies.
plans.more.free.idleBody: After prolonged inactivity, Free may be stopped with prior email notice; prolonged stopped periods may lead to storage deletion.
plans.more.free.zipBody: Folder ZIP downloads must be enabled and exclude protected service state.
plans.more.free.closureBody: Account closure gives you 7 days to export.
plans.more.infra.title: Hoody runs the hardware
plans.more.infra.lede: Bare metal from OVHcloud and Hetzner, fully run by Hoody. Shared plans share hardware and a kernel. Nothing to set up.
plans.more.infra.computersBody: Full Linux computers that keep running when you close the tab.
plans.more.infra.sitesBody: Host sites on your computers. Connect your own domains, HTTPS included.
plans.more.infra.storageBody: Persistent files and saved versions. Connect your cloud drives or laptop folders.
plans.more.infra.kitBody: Built-in tools for you and your AI, each at its own URL. Included with every plan.
plans.more.infra.heavierBody: For heavier work or virtual machines, choose managed bare metal.
plans.more.infra.paymentBody: Prepaid in USD, by card or crypto.
plans.more.trust.title: Who runs your computers
plans.more.trust.managedBody: Bare metal from OVHcloud and Hetzner, fully run by Hoody. Hoody handles the host, security and kernel updates, and hardware monitoring. You control your computers; you never touch a server.
plans.more.trust.encryptionBody: LUKS full-disk encryption is always on, with keys held off the machine. It protects disks at rest; a running host remains accessible to Hoody's platform services. You can encrypt sensitive files with keys you control.
plansLede: Each plan is a server of your own. Its computers share its cores, memory and disk.

faq.addFunds.a: Money you add goes to your wallet. You pay on the provider's page, and the amount has to be inside the range that payment method accepts (shown as From and To). By continuing you agree to the Terms and the Privacy Policy. If the Hub can't tell whether your payment page was set up, Check again repeats the same request to look for it; it never starts a second payment.
faq.stopTracking.a: When a payment or a change may have gone through but the Hub can't tell, it keeps a notice. Stop tracking only clears that notice from this page and lets you try again; for a payment it sends nothing. Check your balance under Wallet & usage or the list first, or ask support whether a payment was credited, because trying again could apply it a second time.
faq.autoRenew.q: What happens when auto-renew is off or a renewal isn't paid?
faq.autoRenew.a: With auto-renew on, a server renews from your wallet at its monthly price. If you turn it off, the server keeps running until the end of the period you have paid for, then it stops. A renewal that isn't paid stops it too. A stopped server is kept for a number of days (shown, when it is known, when you turn auto-renew off) so you can pay to resume it; after that it is permanently deleted.
faq.retrySafe.q: Can I be charged twice if I try again?
faq.retrySafe.a: When the Hub can't confirm a purchase, payment or upgrade, it asks you to check first (Servers for a purchase). Send the same request again repeats that request, so it is never charged twice. A rental is different: Check again on an unconfirmed rental only reads it back, and renting again anyway can give you two servers and two charges. Start a new purchase on an unconfirmed reservation can charge twice too. The Hub asks you to confirm both first. If your browser can't save a new request, it is not sent; if it can't stop two tabs paying twice, the Hub asks you to use a current browser.
faq.upgrade.q: What happens when I upgrade a server's plan?
faq.upgrade.a: An upgrade moves a server to a bigger plan. The server stops, changes and starts again, which takes a few minutes. It pays the difference until the date shown, then the new plan's monthly price comes from your wallet. Upgrades can't be undone: the server can't move back to a smaller plan later. A plan that doesn't keep everything the server has now isn't an upgrade.
faq.freeServer.q: What happens to my free server when I buy or rent?
faq.freeServer.a: You always keep your free server, whatever else you get. Buying or renting adds a new server and your free server stays as it is. Free servers are shared and have limited room.
faq.aiAllowance.q: Where does my AI allowance come from?
faq.aiAllowance.a: Each server you own has its own free AI allowance, shared by every computer on it. The AI usage section lists it per server. If you don't own a server yet there is no allowance to show; a server plan comes with its own free AI.
faq.walletCredit.q: What are Referral credit, Owed and the GitHub bonus in my wallet?
faq.walletCredit.a: Referral credit in your wallet is spent first on servers. If an Owed amount shows, it is paid from new Referral credit. The Wallet credit bonus is one-time: one bonus per Hoody account and one per GitHub account. It can't be added again once claimed, or after the offer ends.
top.why.a: The amount has to be inside the range the payment method accepts. Your wallet updates after the payment goes through on the provider's page.
